title: introduce-jurisdictional-claim-guard-and-audit-consistency-layer
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: tighten enforcement and observability for cross-region/rule-evaluation flows where service claims (operator/service principal) and KMS usage must satisfy jurisdictional constraints. This PR introduces a lightweight policy layer (jurisdictional-claim-guard) that runs as an admission/check step in the RBAC v2 pipeline and a companion audit-consistency-layer that canonicalizes claim->kms mapping in audit events to make downstream compliance queries deterministic.

What this does: - Adds a declarative policy template for jurisdictional claim checks (policy/jurisdiction-guard.rego) that validates operator/service claims against a tenant's allowed geozones and KMS region preferences. - Integrates a KMS claim reconciler service shim (pkg/kms/claim_reconciler.go) that annotates decisions with proof metadata used by audit writers. - Normalizes audit payloads at the writer boundary (pkg/audit/consistent_writer.go) to include canonicalized residency tags, kms_proof_id, and policy_fingerprint. - Adds a feature-flag-driven rollout path (config/flags.yaml) to allow shadow-mode validation and gradual denial enforcement.

Checklist: [x] Policy rego and unit tests [x] Integration tests for audit normalization [x] Backwards-compatible audit schema bump with migration path [x] Feature flag wiring and documentation snippet [x] Perf sanity: guard runs under 200us p95 on common flows

Backward compatibility and rollout: The change ships with shadow-mode enabled by default. For tenants that opt-in, an enforcement toggle flips from shadow->enforce. Audit schema change is additive (adds kms_proof_id and policy_fingerprint) and the writer preserves previous fields. Migration notes included in docs/operational/kms-residency.md.

Risk and mitigations: - Risk: increased latency on auth path. Mitigation: small microbenchmark harness added, guard compiled to a cached decision table for common rules. - Risk: audit processing consumers might not expect new fields. Mitigation: fields are optional and feature-flagged; we communicated to analytics and compliance teams and added a compatibility header.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag 2) Shadow rollout to 10% of operator traffic for 48h 3) Gradual enforcement per-tenant over next 2 weeks with monitoring dashboards for enforcement rejects and audit gap counts.

Notes: This PR focuses on the policy evaluation and audit normalization surface. A follow-up will add an operator UI in the console for policy introspection (ENG-4620).
